title: Storage inspection
learningObjectives: Explain storage inspection and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: The Application or Storage panel lets developers inspect cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, and service worker registrations depending on browser support. Sensitive values should not be copied into logs or shared screenshots.
understand.whyItMatters: Storage inspection helps diagnose stale preferences, cached assets, and persistence bugs. It also reveals whether an application stores more information than it needs.
understand.analogy: The Storage panel is an inventory of browser-side data areas used by the page.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The snippet lists key names only. The developer tools panel provides more complete inspection and editing capabilities.

examples.explanation: The snippet lists key names only. The developer tools panel provides more complete inspection and editing capabilities.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect the application's storage after changing a preference and completing a lesson. Identify the key, value type, and cleanup behaviour.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.

questions.prompt: Which panel commonly exposes localStorage, IndexedDB, and service worker storage?
questions.explanation: The Application/Storage panel exposes browser-side persistence mechanisms.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable engineering workflow?
options: Inspect, validate, document, and verify changes
Assume a successful command means the whole release is healthy

questions.explanation: Reliable workflows use evidence and plan for failure rather than relying on assumptions.
